sara-support: Heads up — overnight CI deploys started failing. Lots of jobs hitting 401 on /v1/deploy. Example from job 2026-04-12_34: 
```
POST /v1/deploy 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"Token expired"}
# headers:
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...
X-Request-Id: r-8f3e
X-Token-Exp: 3218005520
```
Looks like the service-bot token used by the runner expired mid-job. This started after we rolled the runner SA rotation change last night. Can someone triage?

alex-eng: Do we know if the runner uses OIDC (workload identity) or a cached ephemeral SA token? Also paste the job id and pipeline name so I can trace.

sara-support: Job is pipeline: infra/deploy-prod #1423, job id 2026-04-12_34 (same as log). Runner is GitLab self-hosted doing impersonation to project:infra-deploy-sa via our proxy that requests short-lived tokens from token-service. We changed default TTL from 3600 -> 1800 (1h -> 30m) in the rotation config yesterday.

dmitri-ops: I touched the rotation daemon yesterday evening to increase fanout. Did not expect TTL semantics to change. Sharing the command I ran: 
```
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/token-rotator FANOUT=16 ROTATION_TTL=1800
```
That ROTATION_TTL was supposed to be seconds but code reads minutes in the new image; if true we'd be issuing 1800 minutes (~30 days) or 1800 seconds (30 min) depending on parsing — need to confirm.

sara-support: Additional log from the token fetch step right before the deploy that failed: 
```
[2026-04-12T03:12:27Z] token-service: issued token for sa:proj-infra with claims {"iat":3218001920,"exp":3218005520}
[2026-04-12T03:12:30Z] runner: started job 2026-04-12_34 using token exp=3218005520
[2026-04-12T03:12:35Z] deploy: received 401 unauthorized from /v1/deploy
```
Note exp is earlier than the job end time; looks like token lifetime shorter than anticipated. Could be minutes-vs-seconds bug or clock skew.

alex-eng: Can you decode the JWT (no PII) and paste iat/exp? Also check the host clocks on token-service and runner (ntp/systemd-timesyncd). If token iat is in the future vs server time you can get immediate expiry.

dmitri-ops: Quick check on token-service pod: 
```
kubectl -n infra exec -it token-service-0 -- date -u
# outputs: Mon Apr 12 03:11:20 UTC 2026 -> unix 3218001880
```
And the runner host time: `Mon Apr 12 03:12:10 UTC 2026` -> unix 3218001930. Clocks within 50s — not the root cause for a multi-minute TTL.

dmitri-ops: Also inspected SA annotations and rotation config: 
```
kubectl -n infra get sa proj-infra -o yaml | grep token-ttl
  token-ttl: "1800"
```
So the SA annotation is 1800 — but the token-service code expects TTL in seconds, while the rotation config we pushed last week set minutes erroneously in the UI. Looks like a mismatch between UI and backend units.

sara-support: So tokens were actually issued for 30 minutes or 30 *minutes*? The failure log shows exp = 3218005520 and iat = 3218001920 -> ttl = 3600s (1h). But rotation config says 1800. Hmm contradictory.

alex-eng: Wait — exp - iat = 3600s which is 1h. That suggests token-service ignored the new ROTATION_TTL=1800 env and kept default 3600. But logs you pasted earlier show X-Token-Exp 3218005520 which matches 1h. Why are jobs still getting expired? Maybe tokens are being minted earlier but runner caches them and reuses after expiry window. How long between token fetch and job execution?

sara-support: In the failing run, token fetched at 03:05:20 (iat 3218001920) but job started at 03:12:30 — ~7 minutes later. Should be fine for 1h. But we saw exp < job end time in original snippet. Double-checking: I re-sampled another failure: token iat 3218002520 exp 3218002820 -> ttl 300s (5m). So we have mixed TTLs being issued. Looks like multiple token-service replicas with different code versions.

dmitri-ops: Good catch. I rolled token-service image to v2.1 last night but one replica didn't update and remained on v2.0 which used minutes parsing. Running: `kubectl -n infra rollout status deploy/token-service` shows 2/3 updated. That explains mixed TTLs. Fix incoming.

dmitri-ops: Patch applied — forcing a restart on the stuck pod: `kubectl -n infra delete pod token-service-2` -> new pod came up on v2.1. Confirmed all replicas v2.1 and issuing consistent TTL 3600s now.

sara-support: Thanks. What's the mitigation for already queued/running jobs that have a cached short-lived token?

dmitri-ops: Short term: bump the runner side to refresh tokens immediately before each job step. Example script we pushed to the runner image: 
```
# refresh-token.sh
curl -sS -H "X-Service: runner" https://token-service.internal/v1/issue?sa=proj-infra -o /tmp/token.json
export BEARER=$(jq -r .access_token /tmp/token.json)
# then run job step with new BEARER
```
That reduces window for expiry. Medium term: add a token-validation prehook in the pipeline to fail-fast and fetch a fresh token. Long term: fix deploy-time cache invalidation and add canary deploy for token-service image updates.

incident-bot: Created ticket INC-2026-334 and linked oncall dmitri-ops. Priority: P2.

sara-support: Rolled the runner refresh change into a hotfix pipeline; monitored a couple of jobs — deploys completed successfully for the last 12 runs. marking resolved for now, please follow up with postmortem for rollout process to avoid mixed-version issuance. :thumbsup:

alex-eng: Yep — I'll own the postmortem. Will include rollout checklist: verify replica versions, add smoke test that asserts token TTL semantics (decode JWT and assert exp-iat > 1800).

sara-support: Thanks all — closing my ticket on the customer side. :tada:
